newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Boosey upbeat on Disney dispute.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Boosey upbeat on Disney dispute.

text.p: UK music company Boosey & Hawkes Plc said on Tuesday it was confident of a positive outcome in a copyright legal dispute with Walt Disney Co, which is expected to go to appeal in 1997 after an initial ruling in favour of Boosey.

Boosey's chief executive Richard Holland told Reuters it was confident its case about infringement of its copyright on Stravinsky's "The Rite of Spring" in Disney's Fantasia video would be backed again in the U.S. appeal courts. That would open the way for compensation to be made, but Holland refused to quantify the amount at stake.
Earlier on Tuesday, Boosey reported that half-year profits had hit a record high, rising 20.7 percent to 2.05 million stg. The dividend rose 25 percent to 1.91 pence per share.
News that sales had raced ahead in both music publishing and instruments led to the shares being marked up. They were up 20 pence to 782-1/2 by 0830 GMT.

Commenting on the second half outlook, Holland told Reuters that although European markets like France and Germany were likely to remain sluggish, deterring people from splashing out on luxury music items, demand in the Far East and U.S. would make up for it.
"In the Far East sales are up 20-30 percent in some markets," he said.
Boosey's chief said he believed that a greater portion of sales would stem from these growth markets in future. "Long-term, there are so many people there who want to play an instrument."
The group's biggest seller at the moment is the clarinet.

On the integration of its acquisition, Holland said Rico International, a reed manufacturer for clarinets and saxophones, would be "eanrings enhancing for the first four months we've had it. In future there will be synergy benefits as well."
The Bote and Bock buy will be neutral on earnings this year.
This is because the benefits will be cancelled out by restructuring charges, some of which will come in the second half, he said.
